scene 006.5 — birth of layla and needle targeting
scene meta:
location: Breeding Facilities, Landing Site Gamma
time: year 2, month 4, day 12
participants: Ishara, Pazuzu, newborn Layla, Anunnaki overseers, Reptilian guards

Ishara held her newborn and tried not to calculate the probability that this child would live to adulthood in freedom.
The mathematics were not encouraging.
The breeding facilities were efficient, at least.
Clean.
Well-maintained.
The Anunnaki understood that healthy livestock produced better yields.
The Igigi were fed adequately, housed in spaces that mimicked their former homeworld's environmental parameters, given access to medical care that prevented disease from reducing population numbers.
They were treated with the same care one might give valuable breeding animals.
Which, from the Anunnaki perspective, was exactly what they were.
"She's beautiful,"
segments.speaker: Pazuzu

segments.text: "Naming feels like hope,"
segments.speaker: Ishara

segments.text: "Hope is all we have."
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Around them in the breeding chambers, hundreds of other Igigi families existed in various states of reproduction.
The Anunnaki had calculated optimal population growth rates and implemented breeding programs designed to maximize workforce expansion while maintaining genetic diversity.
Pairs were selected based on compatibility matrices.
Reproduction was scheduled according to labor requirements.
Love, when it occurred, was incidental to the mathematics.
"They're preparing work assignments,"
segments.speaker: Pazuzu

segments.text: "What will they have us build?"
segments.speaker: Ishara

segments.text: "Something that will break this world,"
segments.speaker: Pazuzu

segments.text: He was silent for a moment, his mathematical mind processing probabilities and trajectories and the cold equations that governed their existence.
Then: "But there are others here.
Indigenous biologicals.
I've calculated their probable capabilities based on the planetary vrill-signatures I can sense even from inside these facilities.
They're powerful, Ishara.
More powerful than we were when the Anunnaki came for us."
"Will they fight?"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: "Mathematics suggests they will resist. Whether that resistance proves sufficient..."
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: He shrugged, the gesture carrying centuries of defeat. "The Anunnaki have conquered species far more advanced than these stone-entities and their luminescent companions. But perhaps. Perhaps these natives will surprise us."
Ishara looked down at her newborn, at the daughter she had not asked for but would protect with every calculation her mathematical mind could generate.
"I will name her Layla," she decided.
"After the ancient word for 'night' in a language our people spoke before the Anunnaki.
Because she was born in darkness, but perhaps she will live to see dawn."
Pazuzu placed his hand on Ishara's shoulder—a gesture of comfort that predated Anunnaki conquest, that connected them to who they had been before they became livestock.
"Then let us hope, Ishara.
Hope that Layla lives to see freedom.
Hope that these indigenous biologicals prove stronger than we were.
Hope that somewhere in the mathematics of the universe, there exists a probability branch where slavery ends."
Outside the breeding facilities, Reptilian guards marched their patrol routes.
Anunnaki overseers coordinated construction timelines.

And high above in orbital position, Queen Eduhauana calculated resource extraction rates and approved deployment protocols for the network infrastructure that would soon be built across this small blue world.
The harvest was proceeding according to plan.
The indigenous biologicals had not yet noticed the danger descending upon their carefully built Garden.
That would change soon.
end of chapter 006-the first coming
